text:
olivia: Heads up, our dedicated inferencing pool in us-west-2 started failing image pulls after the ECR interface endpoint was created ~10:20 UTC. Tasks show: "failed to resolve registry-<acct>.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com" and `docker pull` times out.

jeff: Is this only ecr.dkr or hitting s3/artifacts too?

olivia: Only ECR right now. S3 pulls (gateway endpoint) are fine.

maria: Can you paste the exact error from the runner? Usually it's either DNS resolving to the ENI private IP or SG blocking ephemeral ports.

olivia: From one node:
```
# docker pull registry-123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/model:latest
Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-.../v2/": dial tcp 10.0.25.42:443: i/o timeout
```
IP 10.0.25.42 is one of the VPC endpoint ENIs for the ECR interface endpoint.

sam: Can you describe the endpoint SGs and node CIDRs? Quick checks:
`aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=network-interface-id,Values=eni-xxxxxxxx` or filter by description `*com.amazonaws.ecr.dkr*`.

jeff: I ran that and grabbed the endpoint SG:
```
SecurityGroups: [ sg-0a1b2c3d ]
sg-0a1b2c3d -> Inbound: 443 tcp from 10.0.0.0/16
```

olivia: Our node subnets are 10.1.0.0/16 (new cluster CIDR from recent migration). So nodes are not in 10.0.0.0/16.

infra-bot: :warning: Detected mismatch: endpoint-sg allows only 10.0.0.0/16, node-subnets 10.1.0.0/16. Traffic to interface endpoint will be dropped.

maria: That explains the i/o timeout (TCP handshake refused/dropped by SG). Important note: Interface endpoints are ENIs with SGs — they require SG ingress rules allowing your client IPs. Gateway endpoints (S3/Dynamo) use route tables and don't have SGs.

sam: Quick options:
- Expand endpoint SG to include 10.1.0.0/16 (fast)
- Add a cluster SG that we can reference (more secure)
- Disable private DNS on that endpoint so nodes resolve to public ECR and go via NAT (not ideal)

jeff: Recommend adding explicit SG rule for the cluster CIDR (10.1.0.0/16) and also add node SG reference. We'll keep least-priv but unblock now.

olivia: On it. Making change in IaC (terraform) and will patch SG manually to restore traffic now.

jeff: Also confirm no NACL blocking ephemeral port range 32768-65535 on that subnet. Interface endpoints use ephemeral source ports from nodes -> check `aws ec2 describe-network-acls`.

olivia: NACLs are clean for the affected subnets (allow all ephemeral). Only SG mismatch.

maria: After SG change, validate with:
```
dig +short registry-123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com
curl -v https://registry-123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/v2/
```
We should see the DNS resolve to endpoint private IP and TLS handshake succeed.

infra-bot: Applied temporary inbound rule: sg-0a1b2c3d allow 443 from 10.1.0.0/16 (manual emergency change). Marking incident tag #ecr-endpoint-sg.

olivia: Confirmed pulls are succeeding again on the pool. `docker pull` completed within normal time.

maria: Please open PR to terraform to add cluster SG reference and update terraform state so we don't lose the manual change. Also add a small test in infra CI that validates endpoint SGs include cluster CIDRs for our clusters (cover drift & migrations).

jeff: I'll create the PR and add an automated check that enumerates VPC endpoints for ECR and asserts SGs permit the cluster subnets (or reference node SG).

sam: Reminder for runbook: when creating interface endpoints, don't assume VPC CIDR; always use SGs that allow current cluster CIDRs or reference cluster/node SGs. Add to eng-infra checklist.

olivia: Thanks all :thumbsup: Closing thread once PR merged.
